one_sentence_story: Francine Shapiro's odd 1989 discovery that tracking horizontal eye movements during recall dulls traumatic distress was vindicated thirty years later when 2019 Nature recordings traced a midbrain-to-thalamus brake that quiets amygdala fear cells while taxing working memory.
so_what_for_you: Respect how dual-task grounding works: pairing rhythmic forward movement or visual tracking with calm reflection keeps one foot anchored in present safety so old alarms don't hijack your whole workspace.
